actual_scope: On the length-9 width-1 cycle, can one positive off-diagonal entry zero a touching Schur entry?
scope_change_reason: Every equal-weight arc meets the touching diameter. The named next step is one sign-flipped neighbor on the length-9 width-1 cycle. The matching positive value is the entry that actually cancels.
bottleneck_link: The periodic caller reuses a width count after elimination. A sign flip keeps the length-9 width-1 bandwidth. Matching the one-vertex fill in both directions is what drops it below the touching diameter.
stop_rule: Stop once the one-entry identities on this cycle are checked. Do not start a width-2 cycle or a boundary-order Gaussian elimination.
evidence: research/length9-positive-rim checks every directed neighbor sign flip. The opposite rim stays -1/16. One entry +1/16 zeros one Schur direction and leaves the other at -1/16. Both directions drop the bandwidth from 2 to 1.
